html:
A soldier from the Kabye people of northern Togo who served in the French army, took part in the 1963 murder of Sylvanus Olympio, seized power on 13 January 1967 and ruled until his death in February 2005.

He ran a one-party state with a cult of his person and an army drawn largely from his own north. Phosphate exports paid for his early years. Pro-democracy protests in 1990 and 1991 forced a national conference and multiparty elections, but he won them all, amid violence and boycotts. When he died he was the longest-serving ruler in Africa, and the army put his son Faure Gnassingbe in his place.
